en.title: Places and directions
en.goal: Ask for and give directions to a place in the city.

lessons.direcoes: Giving directions: left, right, near and far

phrases.scenario: You're lost and need to find the train station. What do you ask someone on the street?
You're giving someone directions and need to tell them to turn left. What do you say?
Someone asks how to get to a place that's straight ahead. What do you answer?
You want to know whether the place you're looking for is far from where you are. What do you ask?

phrases.t: The street is very quiet at night.
The square is in the city center.
The hospital is far from here.

dialogue.title: Asking for information
lines: Excuse me, where is the museum?
Straight ahead, then to the right.

ou-est-vs-il-y-a.title: "Où est...?" or "Il y a...?"
ou-est-vs-il-y-a.body: Use où est...? when you already know the place exists and just want to know where it is (e.g. où est la gare? — where is the station?). Use il y a...? when you don't know whether the place exists nearby (e.g. il y a une pharmacie près d'ici? — is there a pharmacy near here?).

trueFalse.claim: This question is about the price of something.
trueFalse.whyNote: Wrong — c'est loin d'ici ? asks about DISTANCE (loin = far), not price. For price you'd say "c'est combien ?".

review.why: 'la place' = town square / plaza; 'square' is the usual EN word
also 'on the left'; 'to the left' fits both turning and location

review.pt: É sempre em frente, depois à direita.
review.en: Straight ahead, then to the right.
review.why: dropped 'It's' for natural spoken directions; 'It's straight ahead, then to the right' also works
'à cinq minutes' = 5 minutes away (on foot implied); mode of travel not stated
